messages:
elaine: quick idea 12: lightweight "soft-enqueue" layer between frontdoor and admission. instead of 429 during micro-spikes, return 202 + short-lived handle and let an async worker drain a low-priority lane. keeps fast-path latency intact.

josh: interesting. we should define TTL, auth on handle, and how cost is charged.

elaine: TTL 3-6s default per-route. handles HMAC-signed; charge enqueue tokens immediately. per-client enqueue cap and global queue depth per-region.

ravi: fairness: queued items should be scheduled by tenant weight, not pure FIFO. propose a hybrid: weighted round-robin across priority reservoirs.

ops-bot: deploy note: prefer per-edge small queues to avoid cross-node hops. emit telemetry in dry-run mode while still returning 429s.

josh: failure modes: worker crash => claim produces lease_id; complete/abort API; lease TTL + retry cap. also include idempotency keys.

elaine: SDK changes: auto-poll with jitter, expose "in_progress" state. server exposes POST /claim and POST /complete. logging: enqueue_rate, expiry_rate, claim_latency, spoof_rejects.

ravi: security: HMAC handles, nonce + route version to avoid replay/stale claims. ops: alert if expiry_rate > 5% or single client spikes.

josh: migration: dry-run -> per-region flip -> monitor rollback signals. add small perf target: <1% impact on fast-path p50.

elaine: I'll write an RFC with proto sketch, traffic knobs (enqueue_cost_tokens, max_enqueues_per_client, lease_ttl, retry_limit), telemetry, and rollout plan. tagging @josh @ravi for review.
